open_risks.risk: Invalid labels from hidden/off-image geometry or simulator artifacts.
open_risks.mitigation: Block release unless every case has non-null oracle_trace_path, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, fov_supported=true, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and audit images.

open_risks.risk: False novelty if simple heuristics match VLM or human performance.
open_risks.mitigation: Before claims, run blind, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, corridor-width, and largest-floor-patch baselines.

open_risks.risk: T4 answer-space leakage from monotonic body-size physics.
open_risks.mitigation: Report a monotonic-smaller-body baseline, randomize body order, include no-flip controls, and consider asking two independent yes/no body queries instead of one four-way MCQ.

open_risks.risk: Body-width normalization may not remove monocular scale ambiguity from RGB alone.
open_risks.mitigation: Require human sanity, M2b sweep-overlay improvement, and M3 depth-probe results before claiming RGB-local consequence reasoning.

open_risks.risk: T5 is near-redundant with thresholded T1 and may make the benchmark look like a wall-hit detector.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep T5 as a small extension; lead with T1/T2/T4 and use body/action counterfactual pairs.

open_risks.risk: Template-authored examples could be mistaken for benchmark cases in the HTML deliverables.
open_risks.mitigation: Set every current case review to revise; show only simulator-backed reviewed cases, or badge placeholders as not_simulator_validated and keep them out of scoring.

open_risks.risk: A live --runner codex design/HTML round would polish placeholders instead of producing evidence.
open_risks.mitigation: Route to pipeline_verify to generate data_manifest.json, geometry labels, visibility metrics, and visual assets before HTML case review.

open_risks.risk: Hidden or off-image geometry can silently determine labels, especially for T3 and T5.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep T3/T5 extension-only unless visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, fov_supported=true, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and decisive collision evidence is visible.

open_risks.risk: Shortcut baselines may solve drafted cases without swept-volume reasoning.
open_risks.mitigation: Run blind, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, largest-floor-patch, and corridor-width heuristics before empirical claims.

open_risks.risk: T4 can be gamed by monotonic small-body priors.
open_risks.mitigation: Randomize Body A/B order, include flip and no-flip controls, and report counterfactual-pair consistency.

open_risks.risk: False novelty if the benchmark is described as new collision geometry or broad spatial intelligence.
open_risks.mitigation: State that swept-cylinder collision is the deterministic label engine; the contribution is single-frame ego-body action-consequence diagnosis.

motivation: EgoConseq-Bench evaluates whether a vision-language model can infer the visible local physical consequence of its own body executing a short action from one egocentric RGB image. It is not navigation, generic spatial relations, object physics, or hidden-space inference; it isolates body-conditioned ego swept-volume consequence reasoning.

adjudication.rationale: The showcase needs 10 reviewed-surviving cases for each core task before HTML review.

design_principles: Single-image ego-action VQA: one RGB frame, one body description, one action primitive, one answer.
Body is a query-conditioned causal collision operator: do(body=r) can flip the consequence on the same image and action.
Distances are normalized by body width, with 1 body-width = 2r, avoiding absolute monocular metric claims for distance labels.
Labels come from deterministic swept-cylinder geometry and visibility filtering, not LLM judgment.
Core cases must be visible or directly inferable from the current egocentric RGB/depth render: no hidden-corner, off-image, or occluded decisive geometry.
Counterfactual body/action pairs, blind controls, option balancing, and shortcut heuristics are mandatory validity checks.
Swept-cylinder collision is the label engine, not the novelty claim; novelty is the isolated diagnostic of MLLM embodied consequence grounding.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-width forward swept extent
inspired_by: Prior spatial benchmarks only as motivation-to-QA design examples
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Reads how far the queried cylindrical body can move forward before first visible collision, normalized by body width.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible directional swept-volume comparison
inspired_by: VSI-Bench / Thinking in Space only as methodology inspiration
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares candidate visible sweeps in small egocentric angles without route planning or hidden-space inference.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Short composite ego-action consequence
inspired_by: MindCube only as what-if QA construction inspiration, not hidden-space reasoning
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares a small turn-then-forward consequence with straight motion under the same visible-local swept-volume boundary.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-intervention consequence
inspired_by: Counterfactual QA methodology only; the intervention is EgoConseq's do(body=r) collision operator
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Holds image, action direction, and scene-space endpoint fixed while changing radius to test embodiment-sensitive consequence flips and no-flip controls.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible fixed-horizon passability
inspired_by: Prior benchmarks only as coverage-design precedent
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Asks whether a visible forward swept corridor is contact-free for the queried body, without semantic object-physics claims.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move straight forward. How many body-widths can it move before first contact? Options: <2, 2-4, 4-8, >8.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute forward max_safe_distance_body_widths on the radius-specific navmesh and bin into <2 / 2-4 / 4-8 / >8; require visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, fov_supported=true, requires_hidden_geometry=false, collision_point_visible when applicable, and bin_margin_body_widths>=0.5.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Candidate directions: left-front {theta} degrees, straight, right-front {theta} degrees. Rank them by maximum distance before first contact, longest to shortest.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute swept distances for {-theta,0,+theta}, sort descending, require all candidates FOV-supported, and discard near-tie rankings unless ranking_margin_body_widths is sufficient. theta defaults to 30 degrees with 15 degrees allowed.

tasks.question_template: Same RGB and same forward sweep endpoint. Body A radius {r_a} m and Body B radius {r_b} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move straight forward to the same visible endpoint selected for this case. Which bodies complete the action without contact? Options: both bodies, only Body A, only Body B, neither body.
tasks.answer_derivation: At the same pose/action/scene-space endpoint, compare passability across radius-specific navmeshes; randomize body order; generate flip and no-flip controls with counterfactual_group_id and flip_pair_id; report pair consistency. Store endpoint/horizon in metadata and do not let different radii imply different metric travel distances.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Compare A) move straight forward and B) rotate {theta} degrees, then move forward. Which action allows more body-widths before first contact? Options: A, B, about the same.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compare straight max distance with turn-then-forward max distance; label about the same only within tie_margin_body_widths=0.5. Extension-only until FOV support, hidden-geometry filters, and shortcut checks pass.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move forward for {horizon} body-widths within the currently visible region. Is the swept body contact-free? Options: yes, no.
tasks.answer_derivation: Check whether every swept sample through the fixed horizon remains navigable for the radius-specific body. Extension-only until hidden-geometry filters and radius-only/centerline shortcut checks pass.

qa_design.name: Body-Width Forward Horizon
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask how many body widths the queried cylindrical body can move straight forward before first visible contact.

qa_design.name: Visible Directional Sweep Ranking
qa_design.question_pattern: Rank left-front, straight, and right-front swept distances within the current FOV.

qa_design.name: Composite Motion Consequence
qa_design.question_pattern: Compare straight motion with a small turn-then-forward action under the same body constraints.

qa_design.name: Body Counterfactual Sweep
qa_design.question_pattern: Hold RGB, action direction, and scene-space endpoint fixed while changing body radius, then ask which bodies complete the sweep.
qa_design.answer_space: both / only Body A / only Body B / neither

qa_design.name: Visible Passability
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask whether a fixed forward swept horizon in the visible region is contact-free for the queried body.

novelty_positioning: EgoConseq is single-frame, ego-body, action-conditioned consequence VQA; it is not route navigation, active exploration, or long-horizon planning.
The benchmark does not claim novel collision geometry; swept-cylinder intersection is the deterministic label engine.
Compared with PhysBench, it asks about the ego body rather than object or scene physics.
Compared with CapNav, it is one-step visible-local consequence reasoning rather than route-level capability-conditioned navigation.
Compared with TouchSafeBench, it uses a hypothetical action from single RGB rather than multi-view/current collision grounding.
Compared with ENACT and EXPLORE-Bench, it isolates body-width swept-volume collision/passability rather than broad affordance or scene-state evolution.
VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, MindCube, and related spatial-intelligence benchmarks are cited only for benchmark-design discipline and adjacent positioning, not for importing their QA categories.

findings.claim: The current benchmark would be unpublishable if the authored cases are treated as real examples.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path=null, data_manifest=null, surviving_cases=[], case_counts.needs_revision=50, and reviewed_counts=0 for T1-T5.

findings.claim: The design objective is valid only if labels are simulator-generated and visibility-filtered.
findings.evidence: goal.md requires deterministic swept-cylinder geometry, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, collision_point_visible when applicable, requires_hidden_geometry=false, fov_supported=true, and ambiguity filtering.

findings.claim: The drafted cases can currently be solved without ego-body swept-volume reasoning.
findings.evidence: T1 can be attacked by corridor-width or answer priors; T2 by largest visible floor patch or center ray; T3 by left/right layout priors; T4 by smaller-body monotonicity; T5 by thresholded T1.

findings.claim: The showcase requirements are necessary but not sufficient.
findings.evidence: The required fields list includes oracle traces, visibility metrics, heuristic results, and human review, but the exposed cases contain only assumed visibility text and no numeric metadata or assets.

findings.claim: The case taxonomy covers metric measurement, configurational comparison, action simulation, and body counterfactuals only at the template level.
findings.evidence: T1/T2/T3/T4/T5 map to the goal tasks, but no case has simulator validation, so coverage is formal rather than empirical.

findings.claim: Novelty framing is acceptable if kept narrow.
findings.evidence: The blackboard and goal explicitly state that swept-cylinder collision is not the contribution; the contribution is single-frame, ego-body, action-conditioned visible consequence diagnosis.

findings.claim: Freeze the benchmark taxonomy, with T1/T2/T4 as core demo families and T3/T5 as extension families for the current showcase plan.
findings.evidence: goal.md prioritizes T1/T2/T4 for the demo and defines all five tasks as readouts of Body x Action_trajectory intersecting visible scene geometry; input_manifest design_doc marks T1/T2/T4 core and T3/T5 extension.

findings.claim: The design uses VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, and MindCube only as methodology inspiration, not as copied QA taxonomy.
findings.evidence: The adjudicated task layers are EgoConseq-specific: forward swept extent, visible directional sweep comparison, short composite ego-action consequence, body intervention, and visible fixed-horizon passability.

findings.claim: No current illustrative case should be shown as a validated HTML showcase case.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path=null and data_manifest=null; blackboard reports 50 needs_revision cases, 0 surviving cases, and reviewed_counts=0 for T1-T5.

findings.claim: All current case answers, visibility statements, rationales, and H1/H2/H3 empirical claims must be marked not simulator-validated.
findings.evidence: The visible case_author output explicitly states the cases are illustrative placeholders; no M1/M2b/M4/M5/human results or oracle-backed metadata are attached.

findings.claim: A live --runner codex design/HTML round is blocked because it would polish placeholders instead of producing evidence.
findings.evidence: The required showcase fields include rgb_path, depth_path, topdown_path, sweep_overlay_path, oracle_trace_path, visible_sweep_ratio, fov_supported, and requires_hidden_geometry, but the visible cases only contain natural-language assumptions.

findings.claim: The exact next artifact should be a simulator-backed data_manifest.json with visual assets, not another design debate artifact.
findings.evidence: goal.md §9.5 requires deterministic geometry/renderer generation, ambiguity filtering, counterfactual pairing, and data_manifest.json回灌 before benchmark claims.

recommendations: Do not proceed to showcase review until a simulator-backed data_manifest.json exists with non-null RGB/depth/topdown/overlay assets and oracle_trace_path for every case.

Minimum continue gate: at least 60 core T1/T2/T4 cases, M4 oracle >=95%, M5 within 5 percentage points of random, human >=80% and > best VLM by at least 10 points, and oracle-best VLM gap >=20 points.
Run majority, blind, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, corridor-width, and largest-floor-patch baselines before making any benchmark novelty claim.
For H3, report both single-case accuracy and counterfactual-pair consistency; a VLM that keeps the same answer across body flips should fail even if marginal accuracy looks acceptable.
Replace every 'Assumes ...' visibility statement with measured metadata; cases with assumed visibility should be display templates only.
Keep T1/T2/T4 as the demo core. Treat T3/T5 as extension tasks until visibility and shortcut checks pass.
Avoid broad spatial-intelligence taxonomy language in the public framing; keep categories grounded in goal.md swept-volume readouts.
Proceed to pipeline_verify, not further design debate.
Produce data_manifest.json with at least 20 T1, 20 T2, and 20 T4 simulator-backed core cases; add T3/T5 only after visibility gates pass.

For each generated case, include RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, label, max_safe_distance_body_widths, visibility metrics, margins, ambiguity fields, heuristic baseline results, and counterfactual IDs.

After simulator-backed review, produce two HTML files: goal_taxonomy_cases.html with 10 reviewed cases per task, and design_rationale_capabilities.html explaining taxonomy, validity gates, and novelty boundary.
Correct readiness bookkeeping: case_manifest_ready, probe_verified, and showcase_ready should remain false until a real manifest and probe evidence are attached.

Revise T4 generation so the body intervention holds the same scene-space endpoint/horizon fixed; do not let different body radii imply different metric travel distances in the same counterfactual question.
